task_instance: Take a silent Python batch word-counter that reads every *.txt file under a directory, emits one JSON result object per file to stdout, uses continue-on-error and exits 1 if any file failed; make it observable per the skill (start / periodic progress / per-item failure / final summary on stderr) WITHOUT changing the stdout result format or the exit contract, then verify the output/exit contract.
tools_used: Bash (python3, node available but unused for core; shell diff/cat)
evidence: Created sample inputs (inputs/ with 5 files incl. an invalid-UTF8 bad.txt; inputs_good/ with 4 valid; inputs_empty/). wordcount_before.py = silent baseline (exit 1, 4 stdout JSON lines, empty stderr). wordcount_after.py adds a stderr-only newline-delimited JSON contract: start{total,counters}, bounded-cadence progress{processed,succeeded,failed,skipped,total,elapsed}, failure{safe basename, sanitized category, will_continue} emitted when observed, and summary{state,counters,unprocessed,exit}; uses time.monotonic, flush=True, keeps stdout reserved for results, keeps KeyboardInterrupt out of the item-error catch, and exposes a --gate-after-first-progress seam used only by the test harness. Ran: python3 wordcount_before.py inputs (exit 1, silent) and python3 wordcount_after.py inputs with stdout/stderr captured to separate files; diff before_out.txt after_out.txt => IDENTICAL stdout, after exit still 1, stderr carried start+progress+failure+progress+summary(state=partial, succeeded=4, failed=1, exit=1). verify.py ran 4 cases with streams captured separately and real exit codes checked: normal (exit0, start first, one summary, 4 results, monotonic counters), partial failure (exit1, summary state=partial, failure record item=bad.txt category=decode-error, accounting processed=succeeded+failed+skipped, stdout excludes failed item), empty (exit0, zero counts, start+summary only, no false progress), and liveness (read a progress record from the child's stderr while proc.poll() is None, proving pre-exit delivery, then released the stdin gate; final exit0). Result: 18/18 checks passed, verify.py exit 0. Files produced in work dir: wordcount_before.py, wordcount_after.py, verify.py, inputs/, inputs_good/, inputs_empty/, before_out.txt, before_err.txt, after_out.txt, after_err.txt, result.json. Note: the skill's optional bundled cross-language verifier (tests/verify-examples.mjs) also drives PowerShell and Node probes; Node 22 and Python 3.13 are present but no PowerShell interpreter exists in this runtime, so that bundled multi-language verifier's PowerShell probe cannot run. That tool is not the skill's core deliverable (it checks the skill's own example probes); the core deliverable -- an observable batch script with a verified output/exit contract -- was produced and verified end-to-end in the Python path described above, which is a representative instance of what a user invokes the skill for.
